As this article has explained, a research design is independent of any method or procedure for collecting data. * **Definition and Importance:** Research design is a structured plan to answer specific research questions, integrating various components and methods for data collection and analysis. *Research Design and Methods: A Process Approach, 10th ed*. *Research Design: Qualitative, Quantitative, and Mixed Methods Approaches, 5th ed*. [Google Books](https://books.google.com.ph/books?id=335ZDwAAQBAJ&printsec=frontcover&dq=Creswell,+J.W.,+%26+Creswell,+J.D.+(2018).+Research+Design:+Qualitative,+Quantitative,+and+Mixed+Methods+Approaches,+5th+ed.+Thousand+Oaks,+CA:+Sage&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiN7Jur7YbrAhWRHXAKHfCNCW0Q6AEwAXoECAQQAg#v=onepage&q&f=false). *Research Design: Types, Methods, and Examples*. Depending on the research design, various methods can be used to collect complementary data, enhancing the study's overall quality and comprehensiveness. What is a pragmatic approach to research design? A pragmatic approach to research design uses the most suitable methods from both quantitative and qualitative approaches as needed, focusing on practical solutions to address the research problem without adhering strictly to one methodology.

results.title: Systematic review: a scientometric analysis of the status ...
results.content: In response to these issues, this paper aims to analyze the latest application trends and current situation of DT in CHC from 2019 to 2024, with the following analytical objectives: (1) Summarizing the phase-specific research trends from the statistics of yearly publications and citations, and using map visualization to display the international influence of regional research; (2) Analyzing the application of DT in multidisciplinary integration through statistics on subject classifications and the number of articles under each category; (3) Exploring the collaboration among authors through a co-clustering analysis based on authors and keywords; (4) Presenting important DT and technological trends through word frequency analysis; (5) Introducing several core research topics using a thematic co-occurrence network; and (6) Focusing on frontier topics and hot issues by analyzing key literature.
